chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Asim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
It is disliked for the person in ihram to sleep on a yellow bedspread and a yellow elbow-rest. And it is disliked to enter ihram with dirty clothes, unless they are washed. This was narrated.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the person in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the disliked practices for a pilgrim regarding clothing and bedding during ihram?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the makruhat (disliked acts) for a pilgrim in ihram, linking external cleanliness to spiritual readiness by prohibiting sleep on yellow bedding and entering the state with soiled garments unless washed. This reflects the Shia emphasis on both physical purity (taharah) and aesthetic modesty (zuhd) during the sacred rites of Hajj, ensuring the pilgrim's attire remains dignified and free from impurities.
